blocks.text: The **World Bank** is an international organisation that gives **financing, advice and research** to developing nations to help their economic progress. Its main fight is against **poverty**, through development assistance to **middle- and low-income countries**.

blocks.title: What it does
items: Gives qualifying governments **low-interest loans, zero-interest credits and grants** to support their economies
Money helps in areas such as **education, healthcare, public administration, infrastructure and private-sector development**
Shares knowledge through **policy advice, research and analysis, and technical assistance**
Offers advice and training to both the **public and private** sectors

blocks.title: Quick facts
rows: More than **10,000** employees in more than **170** countries, with **189** member countries.
The World Bank and the **IMF** were founded together under the **Bretton Woods Agreement**, with broadly the same aim of serving governments worldwide.
Has grown from one institution into a group of **five** institutions called the **World Bank Group**.

blocks.title: Must-know
blocks.text: World Bank and IMF: both born at **Bretton Woods** and both headquartered in **Washington, D.C.** The World Bank lends for **development**, the IMF protects **monetary stability**.

blocks.title: Five members of the group
rows: International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD)
Interest-free (concessional) loans to governments of poor countries
Investment financing and advisory services for developing countries; the private-sector arm
International Centre for Settlement of Investment Disputes (ICSID)
Promotes foreign direct investment in developing countries through guarantees (insurance)

blocks.title: Who does what in the World Bank Group
items: Soft loans to the poorest countries

blocks.title: Five members: Bank, Aid, Firms, Guarantee, Court
blocks.phrase: Bank for the middle, Aid for the poor, Firms for the private sector, Guarantee for FDI, Court for disputes.
letters: Bank: debt financing to middle-income countries
Aid: interest-free loans to the poorest
Firms: investment finance for the private sector
blocks.note: IDA is the soft loan window of the World Bank, and MIGA is the insurance arm.

blocks.title: Do not mix up
blocks.text: **IDA** is the **soft loan window**, **IFC** deals with the **private sector**, and **MIGA** gives **guarantees**. The IMF is **not** a part of the World Bank Group.

The **IMF** is an organisation of **189 countries** (as per the source) working to foster global monetary cooperation, secure financial stability, ease international trade, promote high employment and sustainable growth, and reduce poverty. It is governed by and accountable to its member countries. Its **headquarters** is in **Washington, D.C.**

blocks.title: Birth of the IMF
items: **Bretton Woods Conference** (officially the UN Monetary and Financial Conference): delegates from **44 nations** met at Bretton Woods, New Hampshire, to set new rules for the post-war monetary system.
Two main results: creation of the **IMF** and the **IBRD**.
The IMF came into being (as per the source, created in 1945).
France became the first borrower from the IMF.
The IMF mandate was updated to cover all macroeconomic and financial sector issues bearing on global stability.

blocks.title: How the IMF works
rows: Keep the **international monetary system** stable: the system of exchange rates and international payments that lets countries transact with each other.
A management team and **17 departments** do its country, policy, analytical and technical work.
Most IMF loan resources come from **member countries**, mainly through payment of **quotas**.
Votes are in proportion to the **quota** of each country, not one country one vote.
Lends only to **member nations** facing difficulties such as balance-of-payments problems.

blocks.title: Bretton Woods numbers
blocks.phrase: Forty-four nations, July first to twenty-second, 1944: two babies born, IMF and IBRD.
letters: Number of nations at the conference

blocks.text: An **SDR** is an **international reserve asset** created by the **IMF in 1969** to supplement the official reserves of its member countries. SDRs can be exchanged for freely usable currencies. Its value is based on a **basket of five key currencies**.

blocks.title: SDR basket: DYPER
blocks.phrase: Don’t Yell, Please Eat Rice: Dollar, Yen, Pound, Euro, Renminbi.

blocks.title: Who controls SDRs?
blocks.text: SDRs are created and managed by the **IMF**, not by the World Bank, ADB or the US Federal Reserve. The Indian rupee is **not** in the basket.

The **IDA** is one of the five institutions of the World Bank Group. It is one of the largest sources of assistance for the world’s **76 poorest countries** (as per the source) and the single largest source of donor funds for **basic social services** in them. It aims to cut poverty with loans and grants that boost growth, reduce inequality and improve living conditions.

blocks.title: How IDA lends
rows: **Concessional**: zero or very low interest charge.
Stretched over **30 to 38 years**, including a **5 to 10 year grace** period.
Given to countries at risk of **debt distress**.
Through the **HIPC Initiative** (Heavily Indebted Poor Countries) and the **MDRI** (Multilateral Debt Relief Initiative).
Primary education, basic health, clean water and sanitation, agriculture, business climate, infrastructure and institutional reforms.

blocks.text: IDA complements the World Bank’s original lending arm, the **IBRD**, which was set up to work as a **self-sustaining business** and lends to middle-income and credit-worthy poor countries. The IDA is administered by the IBRD.

blocks.title: Soft loan window
blocks.text: **IDA = soft loan window** of the World Bank: interest-free or very low interest, long repayment (30 to 38 years), for the poorest countries.

blocks.title: Asian and BRICS development banks
rows: Regional development bank; set up on **19 December 1966**; members of UNESCAP and non-regional developed countries; **68** members (as per the source)
Set up by **Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa (BRICS)**; agreement signed at the **sixth BRICS Summit, Fortaleza (2014)**; BRICS share of votes never below **55%**
Began operations in **January 2016**; **57** founding members; **102** approved members (as per the source); India a member since 2016

blocks.title: What each bank does
rows: Loans, technical assistance, grants and **equity investments** for social and economic development; policy dialogue, advisory services and co-financing. Aims at a prosperous, inclusive, resilient and sustainable Asia and the Pacific, and ending extreme poverty.

Mobilises resources for **infrastructure and sustainable development** projects in BRICS and other emerging and developing economies; offers technical help and exchanges, aiming at environmental and social sustainability. All UN members can join.
Invests in **sustainable infrastructure** and other productive sectors in Asia and beyond to connect people, services and markets. Set up by a multilateral treaty (Articles of Agreement).

blocks.title: Headquarters of the Asian trio
blocks.phrase: Many Sheep Bleat: Manila (Mandaluyong) for ADB, Shanghai for NDB, Beijing for AIIB.
blocks.note: The three Washington, D.C. institutions are the World Bank, IMF and IDA.

blocks.title: BRICS link
blocks.text: NDB = **BRICS** bank (Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa). AIIB = **China-led**, Beijing. ADB = the older (1966), **Manila-based** Asian bank.

sections.title: G-7, G-15, G-20, E-9 and FATF

blocks.title: Groups of countries
rows: Inter-governmental forum of the most advanced economies: **USA, Canada, Germany, Britain, France, Italy, Japan** (and the European Union). Russia joined in **1997** and was expelled after the annexation of Crimea in **2014**.
**Financial Action Task Force**: inter-governmental body founded in **1989** on the G-7’s initiative to develop policies against **money laundering**.
Informal forum to foster cooperation and give input to groups like the WTO, G-20 and G-7. Headquartered in **Geneva**, Switzerland; **18** member states as of June 2021.

**19 countries plus the European Union**; represents about **90%** of global gross national product, **80%** of world trade and **two-thirds** of world population. Began as a Finance Ministers’ forum in **1999**. India is a member.
Forum of **nine** countries formed for UNESCO’s **Education For All (EFA)** initiative. **E** stands for Education.

blocks.title: G-20 members (19 countries, besides the EU)
items: Japan, Mexico, Russia, Saudi Arabia, South Africa
Republic of Korea, Turkey, United Kingdom, United States

blocks.text: As per the source, the 2021 G-20 Summit was to be hosted by Italy (Rome, 30-31 October) and the 2023 summit was hosted by **India**. In 2023 the African Union also joined the G-20 as a permanent member, so check the latest membership.

blocks.title: G-7: CUB-J FIG
blocks.phrase: A CUB munches a Japanese FIG.
blocks.note: Seven countries; Russia is no longer in the group after 2014.

blocks.title: E-9 is alphabetical
blocks.phrase: B-B-C-E-I-I-M-N-P: Bangladesh, Brazil, China, Egypt, India, Indonesia, Mexico, Nigeria, Pakistan.
blocks.note: Just list them in A to Z order; India and Indonesia are neighbours in the list.

blocks.title: The upside-down years
blocks.phrase: 66, 69, 89, 99: only digits that survive a flip! ADB 1966, SDR 1969, FATF 1989, G-20 1999.
letters: G-20 begins as finance ministers’ forum
blocks.note: Digits 6, 9, 8 and 1 stay readable when flipped upside down, so all four years look alike.

blocks.title: Frequently asked pairs
rows: The EU’s non-profit long-term lending institution, set up in **1958** under the Treaty of Rome; headquarters in **Luxembourg**.
Headquartered in **Geneva**; deals with multilateral trade relations, trade policy review and settling trade disputes.
Blockchain Offered New Debt Instrument, issued by the **World Bank**, with the Commonwealth Bank of Australia as organiser and main buyer.

blocks.title: Study tip
blocks.text: Use the headquarters table as a flash card: **Washington** for the big three, **Asia** for ADB, NDB and AIIB, **Geneva** for WTO and G-15, and **Rome** for IFAD.

revision: World Bank: headquartered in **Washington, D.C.**; 189 members (as per the source); fights poverty in middle- and low-income countries.
World Bank Group has **five** members: IBRD, IDA, IFC, ICSID and MIGA.
IBRD lends to middle-income countries; **IDA** gives interest-free loans to poor countries (soft loan window).
**IFC** supports the private sector, **ICSID** arbitrates investment disputes, **MIGA** promotes FDI through guarantees.
IMF and IBRD were created at **Bretton Woods** (1 to 22 July 1944, 44 nations); IMF HQ is **Washington, D.C.**
IMF voting follows **quotas**; its resources come mainly from members’ quotas; it has **17** departments.
**SDR** created in **1969** by the IMF; basket of five currencies; the Renminbi was added in **2016**.
IDA loans run **30 to 38 years** with a 5 to 10 year grace period; IDA serves the 76 poorest countries.
**ADB**: set up 19 December 1966; HQ Mandaluyong, Manila; 68 members (as per the source).
**NDB**: set up by BRICS (2014, Fortaleza); BRICS votes never below 55%; HQ **Shanghai**.
**AIIB**: began January 2016 with 57 founding members; HQ **Beijing**; India a member since 2016.
G-7 has seven countries; Russia was expelled in **2014**. FATF was founded in **1989** to fight money laundering.
G-20: 19 countries plus the EU; began in 1999; **India hosted** the 2023 summit. G-15 HQ is **Geneva**.
E-9 (nine countries) is linked to UNESCO’s **Education For All**.
European Investment Bank: Luxembourg (1958). WTO: Geneva. IFAD: Rome. World Economic Outlook: IMF.
